newFindingsThisCheckpoint.title: ldt-cad-ingest is provisioned with cpu=1/memory=2Gi; the real certified export's working set on disk is ~7.4GB, and Cloud Run's writable filesystem (incl. os.tmpdir()) is memory-backed
evidence: gcloud run jobs describe ldt-cad-ingest --region=us-east4: spec.template...resources.limits = {cpu: '1', memory: '2Gi'}, timeoutSeconds=21600.

download.ts downloadFromGcs and zip.ts extractCadDrop both write to a plain fs path under node:os tmpdir() (cli.ts:315 mkdtemp(tmpdir(), ...)) -- no GCS-FUSE or external volume is mounted at that path per the Dockerfile/job spec.

Wave-1 CP1's own live-verified zip central-directory listing: PROP.TXT 4,895,747,376 B, IMP_DET.TXT 2,065,539,840 B uncompressed (plus the 557,228,168 B zip itself staying on disk during extraction) = ~7.4GB peak local-disk footprint for one run.

Cloud Run (both gen1 and gen2 execution environments) documents its default local/writable filesystem as backed by the instance's allocated memory -- confirmed via `gcloud run jobs update --help`'s own --add-volume text ('in-memory: an ephemeral volume that stores data in the instance's memory... maximum size will be half the total memory limit'), consistent with Cloud Run's long-standing default-filesystem behavior for any path not backed by an explicit non-memory volume type (cloud-storage FUSE is the only such alternative offered, and none is configured here).
newFindingsThisCheckpoint.action: Before executing against the real export, bump the job's resources via `gcloud run jobs update ldt-cad-ingest --region=us-east4 --memory=16Gi --cpu=4` (reversible, no code change, no repo write -- a Cloud Run job resource limit, not a deploy). This is judged in-scope as 'the agent deploys and fixes failed deploys' (OPS-23 program law) applied to the executor's own run of an infra-owned job, not a change to P-169's Dockerfile/cloudbuild/job-creation code. Recorded here rather than discovered by a failed multi-GB run.

newFindingsThisCheckpoint.title: 'staging, then production' is literal for cad-ingest (two real Neon DB targets) but does not apply the same way to factory-parcel-record-fill (mission step 3) -- there is no staging Factory store
evidence: cad-ingest: targetEnv.ts CAD_INGEST_TARGETS=['staging','production'] maps to two distinct secrets, STAGING_NEONDB_URL and PRODUCTION_NEONDB_URL -- a real second database. Executing twice with --target=staging then --target=production is a literal, meaningful two-step per the ingest-freeze decision's own text ('every publish lands on staging before the identical job runs on production').

factory-parcel-record-fill (hauska-factory src/jobs/parcel-record-fill.mjs): reads CAD data via p2-juris-store.mjs neonUrlFromEnv(env), which is HARD-CODED to env.PRODUCTION_NEONDB_URL regardless of any flag (no --target parameter exists on this job at all); writes parcel_record/parcel_record_cell via connectFactory(env) against the single FACTORY_DATABASE_URL secret -- there is no STAGING_FACTORY_DATABASE_URL and no --target flag on this job's parseParcelRecordFillFlags. gcloud run jobs list shows exactly one job, factory-parcel-record-fill -- no staging variant.

Consequence: a cad-ingest --target=staging write does not change anything factory-parcel-record-fill will ever read (it always reads PRODUCTION cad_property). The 'staging' half of the freeze decision's two-step pattern is real and load-bearing for cad-ingest (proves the loader/parser against the real 557MB export without touching the row cad_property serves from); it does not carry over to the fill job, which has exactly one execution target.
newFindingsThisCheckpoint.resolution: Interpreting the mission's 'staging, then production' for parcel-record-fill as AGENT_CONTRACT's own checkpoint model instead: a bounded pilot (CP2, --county=48453 with the job's own targeted-sample mechanism, or a small --per-county/--page-size bound) reviewed before the real full-county --apply run, not a second database target that does not exist for this job. Recorded as a mission-premise correction, not silently substituted -- see contradicted in the close.
